A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Unisolver paper, with 28 readable pages and complete Appendices A–K. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content; differences are confined to administrative version information and PDF metadata.

before.justification: v4 reports original Unisolver experiments on HeterNS, 1D time-dependent PDEs and 2D mixed PDEs in Tables 3–5, plus ablations, generalization studies and other appendix experiments.

after.justification: v5 retains the same original experimental results in the main text and appendices, including benchmark comparisons, ablations and generalization studies.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix H retain identical component embeddings, domain-wise and point-wise conditioning, subspace decoupling, architecture and prediction procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three benchmark collections and retain all appendix scenarios, including equation transfer, incomplete components, unseen viscosity and force, and longer trajectories.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including FNO, PINO, ViT, FactFormer, ICON and MPP in Table 3, PDEformer in Table 4, and DPOT in Table 5. Appendix comparisons also match.

E3.justification: Section 4 and the experimental appendices retain identical splits, sample counts, preprocessing, relative L2 metrics, training and fine-tuning budgets, model configurations and testing procedures.

E4.justification: The embedding and conditioning ablations, incomplete-information tests, joint-training and equation-transfer studies, scalability analyses, efficiency comparisons and trajectory case studies are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions state that HeterNS experiments were repeated three times and report the same standard deviations and confidence levels in Appendix I.6 and Tables 23–24.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted or qualitative findings match. For example, Table 4 retains in-distribution relative L2 errors of 0.0108 for Unisolver and 0.0225 for PDEformer in both versions. Appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, definitions and equations are identical, including Section 3's formulation and Appendix F's analytical string-vibration solution. No mathematical reasoning or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The printed title, abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about complete PDE conditioning, benchmark performance, generalizability and scalability.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are identical. Appendix A retains its qualification about LLM mathematical understanding, while Appendix K retains the grid-data limitation and irregular-mesh future work.

D1.justification: Appendices G–H and I.7 retain identical data-generation instructions, prompts, hyperparameters, hardware and compute disclosures. Embedded code and dataset access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the paper and appendices, and the reference list are identical. No cited work or substantive positioning relative to earlier research changes.

P1.justification: The margin stamp changes from v4, 22 Jul 2025 to v5, 4 Sep 2025. PDF title metadata is corrected to match the title already printed in both versions. Manuscript wording, terminology and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–18, Tables 1–25, captions and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–28 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in the administrative arXiv margin stamp.

improvement.justification: v5 preserves the scientific argument, experimental evidence, statistical reporting, reproducibility information and limitations, including all appendices. The version/date update and title-metadata correction do not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
